description.narrative:
Under Malaysia's ASEAN Chair in 2025, the ASEAN Member States (AMS) have joined hands to promote 2025 the ASEAN Year of Skills (AYOS) to advance the skills and human resource development agenda in the region. Inspired by the success of a similar initiative in Europe - i.e. European Year of Skills in 2022-23, AYOS is positioned as one of the flagship initiatives under the Malaysia’s ASEAN Chair.
AYOS 2025 represents a collective effort to equip ASEAN with a resilient, adaptable, and skilled workforce. The implementation of AYOS 2025 aims to align with, support, and further advance the existing ASEAN Declarations, including the ASEAN Labour Ministers’ Statement on the Future of Work (2019), ASEAN Declaration on Human Resources Development for the Changing World of Work (2020), and the ASEAN Declaration on Promoting Competitiveness, Resilience and Agility of Workers (2023).
The AYOS is being led and coordinated by Malaysia’s Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp.) – a government agency under the Ministry of Human Resources (MoHR), in close coordination with the ASEAN Secretariat, and with the support of AMS, and the ILO as the main technical partner.
The three main deliverables to support the realization of AYOS 2025 objectives are as follow: 1. Development of a Joint Statement on Workforce Skills Development for Future Workforce ASEAN; 2. Design and implementation of an online platform for regional collaboration. This initiative includes the development of a centralized ASEAN-wide online platform to promote skills recognition and mobility.; 3. Public-private partnerships for workforce transformation framework. These initiatives aim to strengthen ASEAN public-private partnerships to equip the ASEAN workforce with skills in demand in the labour market.
As the main technical partner of AYOS, ILO supports Malaysia in the design and delivery of the flagship regional events as well as in promoting alignment with AMS regional & national priorities.
